trigger: A streaming (chunked) update to a time routed alias with a date-math router.start is in flight when an admin replaces the TRA with a plain alias of the same name (DELETEALIAS + CREATEALIAS); the next documents of that request are still processed with the stale RoutedAlias.
reason: Ordinary concurrent client and admin operations are enough. On the first document, TimeRoutedAlias.validateRouteValue (TimeRoutedAlias.java:376-387) copies the alias's current props, adds router.start, and asynchronously writes them with a lambda that ignores the fresh Aliases argument and applies the change to a captured snapshot. So Solr itself writes router.start onto the user's new plain alias (validate-1.log:2636/2786 show collectionAliasProperties={myalias={router.start=...}} persisting), and the same stale-snapshot write can revert any concurrent aliases.json change. The plain alias now has non-empty props but no router.name, so MaintainRoutedAliasCmd passes the empty check and RoutedAlias.fromProps returns null, throwing at MaintainRoutedAliasCmd.java:116-117. The lasting damage is the corrupt alias metadata, which also makes Aliases.isRoutedAlias (Aliases.java:216, prefix match on router.) report the plain alias as routed and changes later CREATEALIAS/CollectionsHandler behaviour (CreateAliasCmd.java:144, CollectionsHandler.java:667).
summary: TimeRoutedAlias.validateRouteValue writes router.start from a stale Aliases snapshot onto whatever the alias currently is, so it corrupts a replacement plain alias (and can overwrite concurrent alias changes); MAINTAINROUTEDALIAS then fails with 'called on non-routed alias'.
